text: Wire the end-to-end read→act→reflect loop through a wrapped Claude session
description: Integrate existing pieces into one closed loop: read top aim (get_prioritized_aims) → act with effector tools (aim A) → write reflection back (addReflection). Runs inside a real wrapped Claude session on a schedule, no streamText middle layer. Depends on A; feeds B.

reflections.outcome: Confirmed the read→act→reflect closed loop is already implemented by the watchdog state machine (cited the exact prompt sites). Marked partially; the only gap is real-world effector actions (6119682f, human-dependent). Did not rebuild.

reflections.lesson: Repeated finding tonight: the autonomy-loop subtree (2b76f62f cluster) is largely BUILT; nearly every 'buildable' open aim there is already realized by the watchdog. The genuine frontier is human-gated (effector credentials) or design-bearing (cooperation-engine UX), not more loop code.

status.comment: The wrapped-session read→act→reflect loop is implemented. The only remaining gap is real-world effector access, which requires a human-selected external system, authorization, and credentials.

reflection: Status reconciliation on 2026-07-30 used the aim’s existing implementation evidence: watchdog discovery, WORKING execution, WRAPPING_UP reflection, scheduling, and recovery are present. Its stated remainder depends on the human-gated effector layer, so `human-dependent` now reflects the actual boundary better than `partially`.
